The parts of a GeoScale and which of them may change

Source: R/tree.R
geoscale_tree.Rd

Lists the parts of a GeoScale as a tree: its properties, the columns of the leaftable, the geometry and the hidden geoframes. Each part carries one of three marks, defined by the identity of the object (geoscale_id()), which is computed from the leaf column, the geoframe names and the region codes:

Usage

geoscale_tree(x)

Arguments

x

A GeoScale.

Value

A data.frame of class scale_tree, one row per part: part, the parent property it belongs to ("" for a property), its kind, shape, mark, the verb that changes it and a note. Printing it draws the tree.

Details

  • fixed: the part enters the identity. Changing it gives another geoscale; the route is to build a new one with geoscale_from_leaftable().

  • derived: the part is computed from another one and is never set.

  • mutable: the part can change and the geoscale stays the same one. The function that changes it is named where there is one.

The marks describe the object; they are not enforced on assignment. str() on a GeoScale prints the same tree.

See also

geoscale_id(), hide_geoframes_geoscale()

Examples

geoscale_tree(geoscale_example())
#> <GeoScale> example@e4024622
#> ├─ leaftable   data.frame [7 x 6]            one row per leaf
#> │  ├─ cell     leaf column          fixed
#> │  ├─ country  frame                fixed
#> │  ├─ state    frame                fixed
#> │  ├─ zone     frame                fixed
#> │  ├─ km2      weight               mutable  geoscale_add_weight()
#> │  └─ pop      weight               mutable  geoscale_add_weight()
#> ├─ geoframes   chr [4]              fixed    country, state, zone, cell
#> ├─ members     list [4]             derived  from leaftable: country 2, state 3, zone 3, cell 7
#> ├─ leaf        chr [1]              fixed    cell
#> ├─ meta        list [5]             mutable  name, desc, weights, default_weight, row_permuted
#> ├─ attributes  data.frame [0 x 10]  mutable  attach_attributes_scale()
#> ├─ aliases     data.frame [0 x 4]   mutable  attach_aliases_scale()
#> ├─ labels      data.frame [0 x 4]   mutable  attach_labels_geoscale()
#> ├─ geometry    NULL                 mutable  attach_geometry_geoscale()
#> └─ hidden      chr [0]              mutable  hide_geoframes_geoscale()
tr <- geoscale_tree(geoscale_example())
tr$part[tr$mark == "fixed"]
#> [1] "cell"      "country"   "state"     "zone"      "geoframes" "leaf"
